**Indikator 11** is a clinical quality indicator that measures the proportion of newly diagnosed patients with atrial fibrillation who develop severe bleeding within one year of their diagnosis [^src1]. It serves as a central metric in the [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] report, which evaluates clinical quality indicators for the treatment and monitoring of atrial fibrillation within the Danish healthcare system [^src1]. 

During the period from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023, the national data for [[danmark|Danmark]] showed that 3.2% (95% CI: 2.9–3.4) of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients developed severe bleeding within one year [^src1]. When broken down by health clusters, regional variations emerge; for instance, [[klynge-vest|Klynge VEST]] recorded a rate of 4.4% (95% CI: 2.3–7.5) for the same one-year period and patient cohort [^src1]. Tracking this indicator enables regional comparisons and helps identify variations in clinical practice and patient safety outcomes across different areas of the country.
